key_insight: The paper introduces UPOM and DU-UPOM to solve inequality-constrained combinatorial optimization without slack variables, reducing qubit/embedding overhead while keeping the method trainable.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for quantum annealing workflows because it lowers constraint-encoding cost and may make practical QUBO formulations for inequality constraints easier to deploy.
method: Combine unbalanced penalization with the Ohzeki method for inequality-constrained COPs.
Replace static penalty coefficients with an auxiliary-variable update scheme.
Deep-unfold the update rule so the step-size schedule is learned from training instances.
evidence_signal: On random knapsack problems, UPOM outperformed original UP, and DU-UPOM found optimal solutions in fewer iterations than fixed-step UPOM and other baselines.
watch_item: The learned schedule and auxiliary update likely need careful training/transfer validation, since performance may depend on the problem distribution and chosen hyperparameters.
paper_title: Slack-Free Deep-Unfolded Combinatorial Optimization Solver for Inequality Constraints
